newsitem.title: BELARUS: Soros Fund pulls out of Belarus over taxes.
newsitem.headline: Soros Fund pulls out of Belarus over taxes.

text.p: The Soros Fund, backed by U.S. tycoon George Soros, pulled out of Belarus on Thursday, saying the authorities had seized $3 million from its bank account in taxes despite previous assurances it would be exempt from tax.

"Today the Belarussian Soros Fund is ceasing its activities because of...financial sanctions against it," the Fund, an international humanitarian foundation which aims to help post-Communist societies, said in a statement faxed to Reuters.
Tax authorities had transferred 77 billion Belarussian roubles ($3 million) from its account at the Belarussian Priorbank to pay the demand, it said.

"This means the Fund can no longer deal with its own bank account," the statement said. "The state authorities insist that violations by the Belarussian Soros Fund are much greater than its assistance in developing Belarussian society."
Belarussian officials were not immediately available for comment.

The Fund, which was awarded tax-exempt status two years ago, said it had spent $13 million on medical, cultural, educational, scientific and economic programmes in the former Soviet republic of 10 million people.
Relations with the authorities worsened in March when Minsk barred its local executive from entering the country.
He was accused of interfering in Belarus's internal affairs and sponsoring the opposition, including the mass media, which criticise President Alexander Lukashenko's authoritarian style of rule.
